_comment: Each benchmark is implemented in three languages (Cangjie/Python/C++).
Each implementation prints exactly two trailing lines to stdout:
The runner verifies CHECKSUM is identical across implementations of the
same benchmark, and uses ELAPSED_MS as the measurement.
Sizes are chosen so the full suite finishes in roughly one minute on a
modern laptop. Override per-benchmark via 'sizes' in this file or via

benchmarks.name: fibonacci
benchmarks.title: Recursive Fibonacci (function call / recursion)
benchmarks.description: Pure recursive fib(N). Stresses function-call overhead and integer arithmetic. No standard-library involvement beyond integers.

benchmarks.name: sort
benchmarks.title: Sort 2M integers (stdlib sort)
benchmarks.description: Generate 2,000,000 deterministic pseudo-random Int64 values then sort ascending using the language's standard sort. Stresses standard library sorting and dynamic arrays.

benchmarks.name: hashmap_ops
benchmarks.title: HashMap insert + lookup (stdlib hash table)
benchmarks.description: Insert N (string,int) pairs then look up the same N keys. Stresses hash maps, string hashing, and string allocation.

benchmarks.name: string_concat
benchmarks.title: String building (stdlib StringBuilder)
benchmarks.description: Build a single large string from N small fragments using the recommended efficient builder for each language. Stresses string buffers and memory growth.

benchmarks.name: mandelbrot
benchmarks.title: Mandelbrot set (numerical kernel)
benchmarks.description: Compute a Mandelbrot escape-time bitmap of size W*W with up to MAX_ITER iterations. Inspired by the Computer Language Benchmarks Game. Stresses tight numeric loops and floating-point arithmetic.

benchmarks.name: nbody
benchmarks.title: N-Body simulation (numerical kernel)
benchmarks.description: Symplectic integrator for the classic 5-body solar system from the Benchmarks Game over N steps. Stresses tight floating-point loops and array indexing.
